newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks say economic, political stability go together.
newsitem.headline: Turks say economic, political stability go together.

text.p: Turkey's top economic officials said they expected no economic crisis this year so long as the established political stability is continued and the government was determined to solve the probelm of high inflation.
"As long as political stability continues, there is no reason for an economic crisis," said State Minister Ufuk Soylemez, in charge of the treasury and privatisation.

"There is harmony between the coalition partners and political stability has been establihed since the coalition took power last year," he told a fast-breaking dinner, referring to the Islamist-led coalition between Welfare Party and the conservative True Path Party.
Ruling out any monetary crisis in 1997, Soylemez said "1997 will be easiest year in terms of domestic or foreign borrowing in the past five years."
Turkey successfully sold a 500 million mark bond on Wednesday in its first foreign borrowing this year which it plans at about $2 billion for the whole year.
Central bank governor Gazi Ercel, who also attended the meal, said Turkey could not live with inflation running at annual levels of 80 percent.
"We have backing from the political power in our bid to lower inflation. A medium-term programme has to be implemented," he said.
Ercel earlier predicted the inflation rate, which was 84.9 percent for the whole 1996, would fall below 70 percent annually in the second half of this year.
"We will overcome the inflation problem. I believe in this," he said.
